edges.effect_quant: The key maintenance trial randomized 89 patients with quiescent ulcerative colitis and found relapse in 4.65% of curcumin users versus 20.51% with placebo over 6 months. A Cochrane review of that same trial judged the direction favorable but the evidence base still small.
edges.population: adults with quiescent ulcerative colitis using oral or enteric-style curcumin adjunctively with mesalamine or sulfasalazine
edges.mechanism: Curcumin can damp NF-kappa B signaling and mucosal inflammatory cytokine activity, which makes it biologically plausible as a remission-maintenance adjunct when baseline disease is already quiet.
edges.summary: Curcumin is one of the more credible supplement-style adjuncts in ulcerative colitis maintenance. The evidence base is still small, but the main randomized trial showed fewer relapses and better activity scores when curcumin was added to standard maintenance therapy.
edges.caveats: This remains adjunctive evidence, not monotherapy evidence, and most of the maintenance signal comes from a single core randomized trial. Formulation and bioavailability almost certainly matter, so generic turmeric use should not be assumed equivalent.
